title: GitOps extension v5 (hermes-gitops.yaml with contractVersion: 5)
description: Contract version 5 of the one file a developer adds beside the agent's manifest. One change over v1alpha4: the optional `runtime` block names the agent runtime the profile runs on and, for runtimes with no upstream manifest, carries the environment requirements. A file without `runtime` is a Hermes profile exactly as under v4 (distribution.yaml stays the manifest and the source of env_requires). With `runtime.kind: eve` the file sits beside an Eve project's package.json at agents/<name>/ and `runtime.envRequires` is the ONLY source of env requirements - there is no distribution.yaml. Everything else (topology, endpoints, requires, apps, communication, deployment, backup, gitAuthSecretRef) is unchanged from v4 and applies to both runtimes.

capabilityName.description: DNS-label capability name. Unique per provider within the compiled catalogue at a given locality.

eventType.description: Versioned event type, e.g. observability.alert/v1. The version suffix is part of the contract: changing the payload shape is a new event type, never a silent widening.

chatopsSpace.description: A ChatOps destination as <connection-alias>#<opaque-destination>. The alias resolves to a provider plugin + credentials in environment/communication.yaml; everything after the first # is passed to that plugin verbatim (a Discord channel ID, a Slack destination, ...). Referencing a space here IS its registration - no separate registry exists.

sessionPolicy.description: How deliveries to an agent handler map onto Hermes sessions. Default when the target declares none: per-event.

mode.description: How deliveries map onto Hermes sessions: per-event = a fresh session per event; keyed = one session per value of `key` (an incident, a workflow); route = one session for the whole route. The generated session key always carries <environment>/<profile>/<route>.

key.description: REQUIRED when mode is keyed: the envelope field the session groups by - `subject`, or a dot-path into the payload (`data.labels.incident`).

deliveryPolicy.description: Delivery semantics for one edge: transport mode plus retry, dead-letter, and ordering behaviour. Declared on a route as its default or on an individual output as an override.

mode.description: direct = publisher -> destination, no broker (does not survive an extended destination outage); queued = publisher -> durable provider -> delivery worker -> destination, at-least-once. queued requires the environment to declare a durableProvider with the matching capabilities (EVENT007 otherwise).

guarantee.description: The only guarantee the platform sells: at-least-once delivery + stable event IDs + destination idempotency. Exactly-once is deliberately not offered.

retry.description: Retry behaviour before an event is given up on. Default when absent: 5 attempts with exponential backoff.

maxAttempts.description: Maximum delivery attempts per event before retries stop.

backoff.description: Delay strategy between attempts: fixed = a constant interval, exponential = a growing interval.

deadLetter.description: What happens to events that exhaust their retries.

enabled.description: Whether exhausted events are kept in a dead-letter queue instead of dropped. Default when absent: true for queued delivery, false for direct.

ordering.description: Optional FIFO ordering, scoped to one output edge and one ordering key.

mode.description: FIFO is scoped to one output edge + one ordering key - never a global order. Different keys process concurrently.

key.description: The envelope field events are ordered by: `subject` or a data dot-path.

onFailure.description: Poison-message policy: block = a failed event blocks later same-key events (strict order over progress); dead-letter-and-continue = after retry exhaustion the event enters the DLQ and the ordering group continues. Default: dead-letter-and-continue.

outputDecl.description: One typed event an app produces: its name, event type, optional payload schema and subject, and the adapter the app emits through.

name.description: DNS-label output name, unique within the owning app. Routes cite it as <app>#<output>.

event.description: The versioned event type this output publishes.

schema.description: Repo-relative path to the event's payload JSON Schema. The publisher validates every payload against it before routing; absent means any JSON body is accepted.

subject.description: Dot-path into the native payload naming the business subject (an incident, a workflow). Becomes envelope.subject - the identity FIFO ordering (key: subject) and keyed sessions group by. Absent or unresolvable: the event has no subject and keyed sessions isolate per event.

adapter.description: How the application hands its native payloads to the platform's publisher ingest.

type.description: How the application hands events to the platform. webhook = the compiler generates a publisher-ingest URL and the app POSTs its native payload there. The only adapter type today.

inject.description: Where the generated publisher-ingest URL is written so the app can reach it.

appValue.description: The producing app's own merged values as the injection destination.

path.description: Dot-path into the PRODUCING app's own merged values where the generated publisher URL lands (e.g. alert.webhookUrl). The app never learns what consumes the event.

agentOutputTarget.description: An agent destination: a named webhook handler on a target profile's gateway, with optional session and delivery policy.

profile.description: Target profile name. The compiler binds only to a webhook handler that profile's OWN contract declares - there is no fallback profile, ever.

handler.description: The named webhook route on the target profile's gateway (config.yaml platforms.webhook routes).

session.description: How this output's deliveries map onto Hermes sessions. Default when absent: per-event.

delivery.description: Per-output override of the route's delivery default.

agent.description: Deliver to an agent: a webhook handler on a target profile's gateway.

delivery.description: Per-output override of the route's delivery default (chatops outputs).

routeOutput.description: Exactly one destination: an agent (profile + handler) or a ChatOps space. Each output is an independent delivery edge with its own delivery ID, retry state, and receipt - one failing edge never blocks another.

routeDecl.description: One declared route: a single event source, optional equality filters, a delivery default, and one or more output destinations.

name.description: DNS-label route name, unique within the file.

from.description: The route's single event source - an output of one of this profile's apps, or one of its external inputs.

app.description: An app declared in THIS profile's apps[].

output.description: An output declared on that app.

externalInput.description: An entry in communication.externalInputs of THIS profile.

filter.description: Equality filters over declared normalized fields (`subject` or data dot-paths). A route delivers only events matching every entry. Filters select among declared routes - a payload can never CREATE a route.

delivery.description: The route's delivery default; individual outputs may override.

outputs.description: The destinations this route delivers to; each entry is an independent delivery edge.

externalInputDecl.description: One verified inbound webhook binding: an external sender POSTs to the shared gateway, which verifies the signature and normalizes the body into a typed event routes can consume.

name.description: DNS-label binding name. Becomes the opaque virtual path /v1/hooks/<binding-id> on the ONE shared webhook gateway - no per-profile public endpoint exists.

event.description: The versioned event type the normalized payload is published as.

schema.description: Repo-relative path to the normalized payload's JSON Schema.

subject.description: Dot-path into the normalized payload naming the business subject (same semantics as an output's subject field).

provider.description: Optional provider normalizer (e.g. github). Absent = the generic normalizer: the verified body IS the event payload.

verification.description: Request-signature verification the gateway enforces on every delivery to this binding.

type.description: Signature scheme the gateway enforces. An unverifiable external input is rejected at compile - this field is required by schema, not just convention.

secretRef.description: Reference to the Kubernetes Secret holding the per-binding signing secret - a reference only, never the value.

name.description: Kubernetes Secret name holding the per-binding signing secret. The secret VALUE never appears in Git, plans, or receipts.

key.description: Key within that Secret whose value is the signing secret.

accepts.description: Optional allowlist of provider event kinds (e.g. issues.opened). Anything else is rejected at the gateway.

dataBoundary.description: The NARROWEST boundary this component's state may leave. Placement says where compute runs; dataBoundary says where the data must stay. The compiler rejects a boundary narrower than the scope the component's consumers span.

endpoint.description: A typed endpoint: a named port on a workload that should have an address, plus who may consume it. The compiler derives the canonical URL and any exposure from this declaration.

name.description: DNS-label endpoint name. Becomes the first hostname label of the canonical URL. Uniqueness within the owning component is enforced by the compiler, not here - uniqueItems only rejects entries identical in every field.

service.description: Kubernetes Service backing this endpoint. REQUIRED on app endpoints (the compiler cross-checks it against the rendered chart under doctor --deep); FORBIDDEN on agent endpoints, which are backed by the agent pod's own Service.

port.description: TCP port the endpoint is served on.

type.description: Who consumes this endpoint: internal = same component, cluster DNS only, never exposed; private = other workloads in the environment; authenticated = a person, behind the identity provider; public = anyone, and ONLY ever explicit; webhook = an external event sender (signature declaration required); external = a named machine client under a service-token policy. Authentication is per-endpoint - v1's profile-level expose.access.policy has no v2 equivalent.

signature.description: Signature-verification scheme the receiver enforces (e.g. hmac-sha256). REQUIRED when type is webhook - an unverifiable webhook endpoint is rejected at compile (TOPO013).

provides.description: Capability this endpoint provides. Consumers cite the capability name in requires[] instead of a literal URL; the compiler binds and injects the resolved URL.

agentEndpoint.description: The endpoint shape with service forbidden: agent endpoints are backed by the agent pod's own Service.

appEndpoint.description: The endpoint shape with service required: app endpoints are backed by a Kubernetes Service the app's chart renders.

contractVersion.description: The authored contract version. Readers dispatch on this key's VALUE: 5 validates here, 4 against v1alpha4, 3 against v1alpha3, 2 against v1alpha2, absent against v1alpha1 - no file is valid under more than one. Emitted records stay markerless - only AUTHORED files carry a version key.

runtime.description: The agent runtime this profile runs on. Absent means Hermes (the legacy runtime), with distribution.yaml as the manifest. Present with kind `eve` means the directory holding this file is an Eve project (package.json + agent/); the project name (package.json `name`, a DNS-1123 label of at most 40 characters) is the profile identity, and envRequires below is the complete environment contract.

kind.description: The runtime. `eve` is the only non-default value; Hermes is selected by omitting the block.

envRequires.description: Every environment variable the agent needs, including its model credential (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY for the Vercel AI Gateway, or a provider key). Same entry shape as the HermesProfile record's envRequires: a bare string means required and secret.

required.description: Absent means REQUIRED - the same conservative default the HermesProfile record applies.

secret.description: A credential rather than configuration. Absent means TRUE.

communication.description: The communication plane: routes from this profile's producer outputs or external inputs to agent handlers and ChatOps spaces. Transport, provider, and credential choices live in environment/communication.yaml - a route here is pure logical intent.

routes.description: The routes this profile declares. The compiler turns each into delivery edges in the generated routing configuration; a route not declared here does not exist.

externalInputs.description: Verified external webhook bindings this profile declares. Routes consume them via from.externalInput.

topology.description: What this profile supports, never where it runs - placement is the environment's decision (environment/topology.yaml), constrained by these declarations.

supportedLayouts.description: Layouts this profile has been designed and validated for. An environment cannot deploy the profile into a layout not listed here (TOPO001). Default when absent: [single].

agent.description: Topology of the agent itself: how many physical instances the compiler creates and the boundary its data may leave.

multiplicity.description: How many physical agent instances the compiler creates. per-agent is meaningless for the agent itself and is rejected here. Default: singleton.

endpoints.description: The agent's own endpoints (backed by the agent pod - no service field). Replaces v1's expose.services with typed entries; a v1 file's expose block is projected onto this shape during adaptation.

capability.description: Name of the capability this entry consumes. The compiler resolves it against the compiled catalogue - a profile endpoint's provides or an environment-declared binding - and injects the resolved URL.

locality.description: Where the provider must be relative to this consumer. Default: global. A same-region requirement that resolves outside the region is a compile error - never a silent fallback.

inject.description: Exactly one destination for the resolved URL: an agent environment variable, or a dot-path into a declared app's values (resolved after placement, before values are emitted).

env.description: Agent environment variable name (convention: HERMES_CAP_<NAME>_URL). Collisions with declared envRequires or another injection are a compile error (TOPO014).

appValue.description: A declared app's merged values as the injection destination: the app to target and the dot-path where the resolved URL lands.

app.description: Name of an app declared in THIS profile's apps[] (TOPO015 rejects an undeclared app).

path.description: Dot-path into the app's merged values where the resolved URL lands.

optional.description: An unsatisfied optional requirement is NOT a compile error: the binding simply does not happen and the injection is absent, reported as an info finding rather than TOPO004. Absent means REQUIRED - the same conservative default envRequires applies. The consuming application must tolerate the variable being unset; declaring optional is a claim about the consumer, not the provider.

requires.description: Capabilities this profile consumes, by name. The compiler fails on a missing provider (TOPO004) and on an ambiguous one (TOPO005); hardcoded cross-profile URLs are the thing this block deletes.

apps.description: The helm apps this profile launches, in author order - v1's shape, plus optional topology and endpoints per entry. Each entry becomes one physical app instance per its multiplicity.

name.description: DNS-label app name, unique within the file.

chart.description: Chart name in the remote helm repo, or (for `repo: local`) the chart's path inside the platform/GitOps chart tree.

repo.description: Helm repo URL (https:// or oci://), or the RESERVED WORD `local`.

version.description: Chart version. REQUIRED for remote repos; FORBIDDEN for `repo: local`.

values.description: Inline chart values - the author's defaults. Fleet defaults and per-instance overrides deep-merge on top; capability injections land last.

valuesRequired.description: Dot-paths into the merged values the OPERATOR must supply. Validated pre-render.

topology.description: This app's instance topology: multiplicity and data boundary. Absent means v1's implicit behaviour (per-agent, target).

multiplicity.description: Default: per-agent (one instance paired with every physical agent instance - v1's implicit behaviour).

endpoints.description: Endpoints this app provides, each backed by a named Kubernetes Service the chart renders.

outputs.description: Typed events this app produces. The compiler generates one publisher-ingest URL per output and injects it at the declared appValue path; communication.routes decide what consumes the event - the app never knows its subscribers.

deployment.description: Agent pod knobs - pod-compute only. baseImageTag is the Hermes image tag (a Hermes profile); runtimeImageTag is the eve-runtime image tag (an Eve agent). Naming the other runtime's tag fails the record validation that follows, never silently.

baseImageTag.description: Tag of the Hermes agent container image this instance runs; overrides the platform's image tag for both the bootstrap initContainer and the main container.

runtimeImageTag.description: Eve agents only: tag of the eve-runtime container image (Node + the pinned eve CLI) this instance builds and runs with; overrides the platform's pinned tag.

diskSizeGb.description: Size in GiB of the instance's data volume claim. Default when absent: 10.

backup.description: Backup intent (unchanged from v1 - schedule + retention only; the destination is a platform concern).

schedule.description: Cron expression for the CronJob that archives the instance's data volume.

retention.description: How many of the newest archives are kept; older ones are pruned. Default when absent: 7.

gitAuthSecretRef.description: Name of a Kubernetes Secret in the instance's own namespace holding the credential to clone a PRIVATE spec.source (unchanged from v1).
